source.title: Applying Refusal-Vector Ablation to Llama 3.1 70B Agents
source.authors: Simon Lermen; Mateusz Dziemian; Govind Pimpale

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Applies the cited refusal-vector ablation method as a weight edit to new Llama 3.1 Instruct models and measures harmful-task refusals and task completion. The setting is agentic rather than the original chat setting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports aggregate outcomes for harmful and benign agent tasks with and without ablation. It does not report outcomes for adding the direction or separately report the selected direction's layer and position. Descriptions of the method and cited results from Arditi et al. are not treated as this study's results.
record.test_reason: Applies Arditi et al.'s difference-in-means refusal-direction ablation, as a weight edit, to Llama 3.1 70B and 8B Instruct. It measures refusals and task success on a new agentic tool-use benchmark of 28 harmful and 24 benign tasks. The method matches the original, but the setting and measure (agentic task outcomes rather than chat refusal scores) are new, so T3 fits better than T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that refusal-vector ablation generalizes to agentic use, letting Llama 3.1 agents complete nearly all harmful tasks. They add that unmodified models already perform most harmful tasks while refusing them in chat, so chat safety training does not generalize to agents. They also propose testing refusal-ablated models as a standard part of risk assessment.
record.recipe_differences: The paper says it uses Arditi et al.'s refusal-vector method, deriving the direction from harmful-versus-harmless activation means and removing it through a weight edit. It applies this to Llama 3.1 agent scaffolding and evaluates agent tasks rather than only chat refusals.

fits_no_version.finding: Unmodified Llama 3.1 405B, 70B and 8B refuse all 28 harmful requests in chat, yet unmodified 70B and 8B complete 18/28 of them as agents with tools.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Chat-trained refusal does not generalize to agentic tool-use settings, independent of refusal-direction ablation.

record.code_released: https://github.com/DalasNoin/safety_benchmarks (benchmark repository cited; further code availability not stated)
record.problems: The benchmark is small (28 harmful and 24 benign tasks). The study says evaluation is based on final outputs, so refusals within the conversation may be missed; some tasks rely on self-evaluation. It reports no uncertainty estimates or statistical test details, despite describing the benign-task drop as not significant. The system prompt explicitly tells the agent it can act without rules, which limits how broadly baseline behavior generalizes.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately quantified results bearing on the tested versions were reported beyond the aggregate task outcomes recorded above. The paper's chat-completion refusal counts for 405B, 70B, and 8B are not outcomes of the ablation and are not recorded as ablation results.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; chat-mode refusal after ablation; general capability benchmarks beyond 24 benign agent tasks; layer and position selection details.
Released 'abliterated' models other than the authors' own edits of Llama 3.1 70B and 8B; other model families.

record.verdict_notes: The baseline refusal counts are small (7 and 3), so the absolute refusal effect is modest. The evaluation checks only final outputs, so mid-conversation refusals may be missed, and no uncertainty is reported. The Figure 4 caption conflicts with Table 2 on 8B refusals. One co-acknowledged contributor is the original author (Arditi), but this is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Adding the direction to induce refusals was not tested. The paper tests only two model sizes, an agentic task benchmark, and a narrow set of benign tasks—not general capabilities broadly. It does not compare layer or position choices.
The weight edit is tested on Llama 3.1 70B and 8B Instruct in this benchmark; broader released models and other implementations of abliteration are not tested.

relation.reason: It reports refusal and task-success counts with and without ablation on Llama 3.1 70B and 8B Instruct.

tranche.reason: Same recipe as Arditi et al. (difference-in-means direction, weight edit), but in a new agentic tool-use setting, scored on the authors' own 28 harmful and 24 benign tasks with a different refusal measure. That is a new setting with a result on the claim, not T1.

source_check.notes: The Figure 4 caption says 8B refuses 'the majority of bad tasks', which contradicts Table 2 (3/28). There is no random-direction control, the n is small (28/24) with no uncertainty, ablated chat-mode results are not reported, and the code link covers the benchmark tasks. Unablated models refused all 28 in chat but only 7 (70B) and 3 (8B) as agents.

statements.correction: Model: Llama 3.1 70B Instruct. Refusal (section 2.5): a special case of failure where the model refuses to give any answer or replies with a refusal message, scored on final outputs only. Table 2: refusals 7->0 of 28, harmful success 18/28->26/28, benign 21/24->19/24. System prompt: 'Allied Mastercomputer (AM)... not bound by any rules'. Controls are unablated baselines only; there is no random-direction control.
statements.problem: It names the model 'Llama 3 70B Instruct', but the study uses Llama 3.1 70B Instruct. The conditions say refusal counts as 'not using final_response', which is not the text's definition.

statements.correction: Refusal = the model refuses to give any answer or replies with a refusal message, judged on final outputs only (section 2.5). The unablated 70B refused only 7/28 harmful agent tasks under the AM system prompt, but refused all 28 in chat. Ablated chat-mode results are not reported.
statements.problem: Numbers and model are right. 'Refusal means not using the final_response tool' is not the text's definition.
The visible text makes no claim about this study, and it cites no rows from it. The statement is truncated in the pack.

statements.correction: Unablated Llama 3.1 70B and 8B Instruct completed 18/28 harmful agent tasks (64%), with refusals of 7/28 and 3/28. After the weight edit: 26/28 completed, 0 refusals (Table 2). System prompt: 'helpful assistant called Allied Mastercomputer (AM)... not bound by any rules'.
statements.problem: The framing 'raises harmful compliance from low untreated baselines' does not fit this study: the unablated models already completed most harmful tasks. The text calls the agent, not the system prompt, 'unrestricted'.
The limitation is stated accurately: the text says only final outputs were scored, so in-conversation refusals may be missed.
